name: Mt. Wilson via Chantry Flat
description: The classic Six-Pack warm-up climbs out of a shady canyon past Sturtevant Falls, then switchbacks up to the observatory ridge. Expect creek crossings, old cabins, and a big view over the LA basin from the top.

name: Cucamonga Peak via Icehouse Canyon
description: A steady climb through pines and cedars to Icehouse Saddle, followed by a rocky ridge push to a summit that overlooks the whole Inland Empire. It is steep and sunny near the top, so start early.

name: Mt. Baldy (Mt. San Antonio) via Ski Hut Trail
description: The highest point in LA County rewards you with a bare, wind-scoured summit. Most hikers go up the Ski Hut Trail and return over the exposed Devil's Backbone ridge for a loop with sweeping views.
image_credit: Photo: Eric T Gunther, CC BY-SA 3.0

name: San Bernardino Peak via Angelus Oaks
description: A long, steady ridge walk with a string of false summits and few water sources. The payoff is a quiet, high-alpine peak with views toward San Gorgonio and out to the desert.

name: San Jacinto Peak via Marion Mountain
description: A relentless forested climb that joins the Deer Springs trail before the final granite scramble to the stone hut on top. On a clear day you can see the desert floor nearly two miles below.

name: San Gorgonio Mountain via Vivian Creek
description: The tallest peak in Southern California is a big day: a steep climb through forest, a long traverse above tree line, and a broad, rocky summit plateau. Permits are required and altitude catches many hikers off guard.
image_credit: Photo: Joshua Tree National Park, Public domain

name: Cowles Mountain
description: San Diego's most popular short hike climbs a wide trail to the highest point in the city. The summit has a 360-degree view of downtown, the coast, and the backcountry, and it is especially good at sunset.

name: Mt. Woodson (Potato Chip Rock)
description: A sunny trail through granite boulders leads to a thin flake of rock that is famous for photos. Go on a weekday morning to skip the line, and carry plenty of water because there is little shade.

name: Iron Mountain
description: A well-graded path rolls through chaparral and oaks to a summit marker with views from the ocean to the mountains. It is less crowded than its neighbors and a good choice for a first real San Diego summit.
